question.problem: In a right triangle $△LMN,$ $∠M$ is a right angle, $MN=\sqrt{5}$ and $LM=\sqrt{11}.$ Determine the cosine of $∠N.$
question.worked_solution:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224552/assets/df7dcd343dd2676cb38b7df3c2d8cb599fed45b9c0b25194609effe2bf27a6f7.png)

Recall the definition of cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡N=\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}=\frac{MN}{LN}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{LN}
$$

Here, we need to determine the missing length $LN.$ The trick is to use the Pythagorean Theorem:

$$
\begin{aligned}LN & =\sqrt{M{N}^{2}+L{M}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(\sqrt{5})^{2}+(\sqrt{11})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5+11} \\  & =\sqrt{16} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡N & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{LN}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
